newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran cleric welcomes Afghan pact against Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric welcomes Afghan pact against Taleban.

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric on Friday welcomed a pact by factions opposed to Afghanistan's ruling Taleban, expressing hope that the coalition would defeat the militant Sunni Moslem militia.

"We are glad that, on the one hand, that Afghan groups have come to their senses now, have set up (joint) headquarters and protecting and helping each other," Ayatollah Mohammad Emami Kashani said in a mass prayer sermon broadcast on Tehran radio.
"We are also happy the Taleban forces are losing their power," said Emami Kashani who is a member of the powerful Guardian Council.
He was referring to the military pact signed on Thursday by Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum, ousted government military head Ahmad Shah Masood and a leader of a Shi'ite Moslem faction.

"We hope that, with God's help, Afghanistan's Moslem people will win and this force...which is backed by America will be defeated and that again the White House will be exposed...," he told worshippers who responded by chanting "Death to America".
Emami Kashani blasted the Taleban for giving Islam a bad name by closing girls schools, preventing women from working and requiring men to grow beards.

Shi'ite Iran recognises the government of Burhanuddin Rabbani, ousted by the Taleban two weeks ago, as legitimate. Iranian media have condemned Taleban as manipulated by the United States, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has criticised the Taleban as "un-Islamic".
An Afghan foreign ministry official said on Friday Iran provoked the Taleban government by repeated criticism of the Taleban despite recent assurances that relations would improve.
